mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 1 Series 120i engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 120i engine replacement typically costs £1,195-£3,200 for a reconditioned or rebuilt unit supply-only, depending on the engine code. With supply and fit, expect £2,300-£4,000 depending on the specialist and location.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 120i?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common warning signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 1 Series 120i (N43 and N13 engines) include a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, rough idling, poor engine performance, and in later stages, the engine management light illuminating.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 1 Series 120i?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 2007-2016 BMW 1 Series 120i is typically valued at £3,000-£8,000. If your 120i is worth under £4,500, a full rebuilt engine may not be economically viable - consider a used engine or scrap the car. If your car is worth £6,000+ (low mileage, M Sport spec, good condition), a reconditioned engine with warranty is a sound investment.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 1 Series 120i engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 1 Series 120i engine replacement typically takes 2-3 days for a specialist to complete, including removal of the old unit and fitting the replacement. Timing chain replacement alone (without full engine removal) can be completed in 1-2 days.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the BMW 120i and 118i?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both the BMW 120i and 118i share engine families but with different power outputs and sometimes different engine capacities. The 118i produces 127-140 hp depending on generation, while the 120i produces 150-184 hp.

mainEntity.name: Does a BMW 1 Series 120i rebuilt engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt BMW 1 Series 120i engine supplied through EnginesMarket comes with a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers the engine against manufacturing defects and component failure, giving you peace of mind when investing in a replacement N46, N43, N13 or B48 unit.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 1 Series 120i - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 120i has been a popular petrol model across three generations of the 1 Series in the UK, offering a step up in power from the 118i without the running costs of the six-cylinder 125i and 130i. Launched with the first-generation E87 in 2004, it has evolved from a naturally aspirated 2.0-litre four-cylinder to a 1.6-litre turbo, and finally to a modern 2.0-litre turbocharged B48 unit. The 120i badge represents the sweet spot between accessible performance and everyday usability.

milestones.description: N46B20B, 2.0L naturally aspirated I4, 150 hp, launched with the E87 five-door and E81 three-door 1 Series
N43B20O0, 2.0L naturally aspirated I4 with direct injection, 170 hp, introduced as part of the E87/E81 LCI update
N13B16M0, 1.6L turbocharged I4, 177 hp, launched with the second-generation F20/F21 1 Series
B48B20M0, 2.0L turbocharged I4, 184 hp, introduced as part of the F20/F21 LCI update
F40 generation launches with B48A20A, 2.0L turbocharged I4, 178 hp, continuing the 120i badge
Current F70 generation continues with updated B-series petrol engines

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 1 Series 120i is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

items.title: 2.0L Naturally Aspirated Petrol (2004-2007)
items.commonFailure: The N46 engine can suffer from timing chain tensioner failure, VANOS seal issues, and valve stem seal wear leading to oil consumption. The original tensioner was too short and allowed the chain to become slack, which would then rub and clatter against the guides. Oil consumption of 1 litre per 300 miles has been reported on higher-mileage examples. Typical failure mileage: 80,000-120,000 miles.

items.title: 2.0L Naturally Aspirated Petrol (2007-2011)
items.commonFailure: The N43 engine suffers from timing chain guide fragmentation - plastic pieces can end up in the oil pickup leading to oil starvation. The N43 also suffers from injector, EGR and water pump issues, as well as NOx sensor problems. Typical failure mileage: 40,000-100,000 miles. This engine is known to be less reliable than its predecessor.
items.cta: -> Get quotes for N43B20O0 BMW 1 Series 120i engine replacement
items.closing: -> Get quotes for N43B20O0 BMW 1 Series 120i engine replacement

items.title: 1.6L Turbocharged Petrol (2011-2016)
items.commonFailure: The N13 engine (part of the Prince engine family) suffers from timing chain tensioner and guide failure, a well-documented issue across the N13, N20, N43 and N47 engine families. The timing chain is known to stretch and snap, which can cause significant damage to the engine. Oil consumption and high-pressure fuel pump failure are also common. Typical failure mileage: 50,000-80,000 miles.

items.title: 2.0L Turbocharged Petrol (2016-2019)
items.commonFailure: The B48 is BMW's most modern four-cylinder petrol engine and is generally reliable. Widespread B48 timing chain failures are not a known pattern, though individual failures can occur. Coolant leaks from the coolant flange pipe have been reported, and like all direct-injection engines, carbon buildup on intake valves can occur over time. The B48 uses a timing chain rather than a belt.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 1 Series 120i Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: H3: The BMW 1 Series 120i has been powered by five different petrol engines across its production life, each with its own character and weaknesses. Early cars (2004-2007) use the N46B20B - a 2.0-litre naturally aspirated unit that can suffer from timing chain wear and oil consumption. The N43B20O0 (2007-2011) introduced direct injection but brought timing chain guide fragmentation and multiple sensor issues. The N13 turbo (2011-2016) offered 177 hp but inherited timing chain problems from the Prince engine family. Later B48-powered cars (2016-present) are the most reliable of the bunch, with no widespread timing chain failure pattern. Replacement demand for the BMW 120i is driven primarily by N43 and N13 timing chain failure. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Guide Failure - Why the BMW 1 Series 120i N43 and N13 Engines Fail Prematurely
problems.rootCause: The timing chain guides on BMW's N43 and N13 petrol engines were made of plastic that becomes brittle with age and heat. On the N43, the guides can break and fragment, with debris falling into the sump and blocking the oil pump intake - leading to oil starvation and engine seizure. On the N13, the timing chain is known to stretch and snap. Because both engines are of interference type, a stretched or snapped timing chain can cause pistons to collide with valves - resulting in catastrophic engine failure.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides and VANOS units
repairOptions.longevity: Best if caught early - rattle present but engine still running

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: When chain has snapped or engine is already damaged

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2007-2016 BMW 1 Series 120i is currently valued at approximately £3,000-£8,000 depending on mileage, condition and generation [THIRD-PARTY - Auto Trader / Parkers market observation]. This places the 120i in the "repair or used engine typically makes more sense than a full rebuilt unit" bracket for lower-value examples. If your 120i is worth under £4,500 and the engine has suffered catastrophic timing chain failure, evaluate scrap value first - replacement cost may approach or exceed the car's market value. For well-maintained, higher-spec examples (M Sport, low mileage, later generation) worth £6,000+, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with warranty is a viable investment.
problems.recommendation: If you hear the characteristic rattling noise from the timing chain on cold start in your N43 or N13-powered BMW 120i, act immediately. An £800-£1,300 specialist timing chain replacement is far cheaper than a full engine rebuild. If the chain has already snapped, the repair bill often exceeds the car's value - in that scenario, compare rebuilt engine prices through EnginesMarket against the cost of replacing the car. For owners planning to keep their 120i for 2+ years, a reconditioned N43 or N13 with upgraded timing components and warranty offers genuine peace of mind.

problems.group: Oil Consumption & Valve Stem Seal Wear
problems.h4: Oil Consumption & Valve Stem Seal Wear - N46 and N43 Engines
problems.rootCause: The N46 and N43 engines can suffer from worn valve stem seals, leading to excessive oil consumption. This is often accompanied by blue smoke on start-up and a gradual increase in oil usage between services. The N46 in particular has been reported to use 1 litre of oil per 300 miles when the seals are badly worn.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace valve stem seals without removing cylinder head (specialist tooling)
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught before other damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with new seals, guides and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: If oil consumption is severe and compression is low

problems.recommendation: Oil consumption of 1 litre per 1,000 miles or more warrants investigation. A specialist valve stem seal replacement using the "in-situ" method (without cylinder head removal) is often the most cost-effective solution for the BMW 1 Series 120i. If combined with timing chain wear, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded components may offer better long-term value.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt BMW 1 Series 120i engine prices

problems.h4: B48 Engine - Coolant Leaks and General Reliability
problems.rootCause: The B48 is generally a reliable engine, but owners report coolant leaks, particularly from the coolant flange pipe. Carbon buildup on intake valves can occur due to direct injection, and some owners have reported cracked pistons in tuned examples. Widespread B48 timing chain failures are not a known pattern.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace coolant flange pipe and seals
Media blasting to remove carbon deposits from intake valves
Complete rebuilt unit with new components

problems.recommendation: The B48 is BMW's most advanced four-cylinder petrol engine and is generally reliable with proper maintenance. Coolant leaks should be addressed promptly to prevent overheating. Carbon buildup is a maintenance issue rather than a catastrophic failure point - regular high-speed driving can help reduce deposits, but professional cleaning is sometimes necessary. If you're considering a remap, be aware that tuned B48 engines have been known to suffer from cracked pistons.

finalCta.h4: Don't Let Engine Failure Write Off Your BMW 1 Series 120i
finalCta.paragraph: The N43 and N13 engines in your BMW 120i have known timing chain weaknesses - but with the right specialist, these can be addressed before catastrophic failure occurs. Later B48-powered cars are more reliable but still benefit from regular maintenance and vigilance for coolant leaks.
